title: Incorrect definition for media element pseudo class `:stalled`

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

We (Mozilla) believe that the definition of [`:stalled`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics-other.html#selector-stalled) might be incorrect. From [this test](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/feefed22c39dfd86ec2468960366db989c8a6fbd/testing/web-platform/tests/css/selectors/media/media-loading-state-timing.sub.html#27), it appears that this selector is intended to correspond to the media element’s `stalled` event. However, its definition conflicts with how the `stalled` event is defined in the HTML spec.

First, let see the selector definition.
```
:buffering
The :buffering pseudo-class must match all media elements whose paused attribute is false, networkState attribute is NETWORK_LOADING, and ready state is HAVE_CURRENT_DATA or less.

:stalled
The :stalled pseudo-class must match all media elements that match the :buffering pseudo-class and whose is currently stalled is true.
```

So the `:stalled` selector is required to match `:buffering`, which means the **readyState must be HAVE_CURRENT_DATA or less**. However, in the HTML spec, the `stalled` event is related to [downloading](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#event-media-stalled) only, not related with the ready state.  

A media element could already have enough data buffered and then encountering an issue for not being able to download more data, which would trigger `stalled`. That does not necessarily mean the ready state must be equal to or below `HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`.

Because of this, I think it is incorrect for `:stalled` to require matching `:buffering`. Instead, it should likely only check `networkState` and `paused`, but not `readyState`.

----

Media pseudo-classes are [included in Interop this year](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1003), so we should ensure their definitions are correct. @foolip @heycam, would you mind sharing your thoughts on this?

FYI, Firefox also has an [implementation of media pseudo-classes](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1707584) available in Nightly, which is currently disabled by default.
